title: Label Variant Consolidation — Thought Log
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal record of ideas and heuristics for consolidating label variants across multiple annotation batches. Trying to capture emergent patterns, micro-rules, and prioritization so we can make an initial automated normalization pass and a shortlist of cases that must go to human adjudication.

Summary of problem:
We have a long tail of semantically identical labels that differ orthographically or by granularity. Examples collected from query dataset v3: 
- address | addr | addr. | AddressLine | mailing_address
- phone | tel | phone_number | ph num | +1-212-555-1212 (formats)
- org | organization | company | company-name | corp
- email | e-mail | email_address
- person | person_name | p_name | user_name

Impacts observed:
- Training signals diluted when same semantic class split across tags.
- Post-label aggregation and analytics produce inflated distinct-entity counts.
- Model evaluation shows higher variance on metrics where consolidated label has lower support per variant.

First-pass consolidation heuristics (automatable):
1) Case-fold + strip punctuation: convert 'ADDR.' and 'addr' -> 'addr' as a canonical fold.
2) Common synonyms map: maintain a small dictionary: {"organization": "org", "company": "org", "corp": "org"} — seed from frequent counts.
3) Numeric-normalization for phones: remove formatting and country code heuristics (keep +country separate).
4) Compound-to-base mapping: 'address_line' -> 'address' if sample-level evidence shows same span semantics.
5) Abbreviation expansion list (addr -> address, tel -> phone) but mark expansions with confidence score.

Edge / ambiguous cases (flag for adjudication):
- Overloaded words: 'account' could be financial account vs user-account vs social-handle; context needed.
- Hierarchical labels: 'person' vs 'author' vs 'speaker' — decide whether to merge or keep separate depending on downstream needs.
- Overlapping spans: 'The Redwoods' might be tagged as ORG or LOC in different passes. Use contextual rules (prepositions, suffix tokens) to disambiguate but mark for manual review if rule confidence low.
- Tokens that look like labels inside code/config (e.g., 'addr:' in logs) — need separate treatment to avoid false positives.

Heuristic confidence scoring (proposed):
- Frequency score: how many times variant occurs across pooled datasets (higher -> safer to map).
- String-similarity score: edit-distance + token overlap.
- Contextual divergence: measure average token-context embedding similarity between variant instances; if high variance -> flag.
- Label co-occurrence: variants that co-occur with same adjacent labels -> likely same class.

Example rule pipeline (implementation sketch):
1) Ingest labels and raw spans from all batches.
2) Normalize (case, punctuation, unicode NFC).
3) Collapse trivial variants (addr/addr. etc).
4) Apply synonym map (dictionary) where frequency score > threshold.
5) Compute contextual embedding similarity for remaining low-confidence mappings; if similarity > 0.82 and frequency > 20 -> auto-merge.
6) Anything with low frequency or low similarity -> assign to "adjudication queue".

Sampling & adjudication policy:
- For every auto-merge decision, sample 20 examples and surface to human reviewer to catch systematic errors early.
- Maintain an adjudication queue prioritized by: downstream impact (eval flakiness), frequency, and novelty (new tokens unseen before).

Metrics to track post-normalization:
- Variant collapse ratio (pre / post distinct label count).
- Flip-rate: percent of spans whose canonical label changed by auto-merge.
- Adjudication throughput and false-positive rate from sampled checks.
- Model performance delta on a held-out eval set (F1/precision/recall per canonical label).

Samples of tricky real instances (copied from dataset) — these should be preserved in a canonical examples sheet: 
1) "john.doe_at_example.com" labeled as 'email' vs 'username' in different batches.
2) "Redwood Inc.," labeled ORG vs ORG+punct.
3) "+44 7700 900123" versus "07700 900123": country code presence affects downstream normalization.
4) "billing address" vs "Address" vs span "123 Main St" (structure vs label text confusion).

Operational notes / quick wins:
- Add a lightweight validator into the labeling UI: when a new free-text label is entered, compute nearest canonical candidate and prompt: "Map to \"address\"?" with 'yes/define new' options. This would reduce new variant proliferation.
- Ship a nightly job that builds variant frequency tables and pushes top-50 likely merges to a review board.
- Provide label authors with the top-5 canonical mappings and brief examples at label creation time.

Open questions / hard decisions:
- When should two similar labels remain separate classes? Criteria proposal: if there is at least N=50 high-confidence spans showing different downstream behavior (e.g., different entity-level attributes, different coreference patterns), keep separate. Need to test sensitivity.
- How to treat multi-word vs single-token variants ("first name" vs "given_name"). Are these just synonyms or indicate different schema?
- Internationalization: address formats differ by country; collapsing globally may hide locale-specific needs. Should we maintain per-locale canonicalization?

Action items (next short cycles):
- Samir to prototype frequency + string-similarity merge script (LABEL-PR-01) — due 2024-11-20.
- Eleanor to prepare adjudication UI mockups and list of initial prompt strings for in-UI mapping suggestions — due 2024-12-01.
- I (Maya) to compile a preliminary canonical map seed (top 200 variants) and run an internal sampling audit.

Notes to self / miscellaneous brain-dump:
- Watch out for 'snake_case' vs 'kebab-case' vs 'camelCase' label inputs from dev-samples. Convert all to a single presentation form for analytics, but store original label verbatim for provenance.
- Keep provenance: for every auto-merge, store evidence (sample spans, frequency, similarity metrics) so we can revert decisions if downstream signals diverge.
- Consider lightweight ML classifier (fastText or small transformer) to predict canonical mapping when heuristics conflict; use human-in-the-loop for low-confidence predictions.

References & pointers:
- Confluence guideline draft (linked above) — review section 3 for label lifecycle.
- Slack thread #labeling: recent discussion pinned around 'addr' expansion.
- JIRA-LABEL-682: customer report where inconsistent labeling caused metric drift in product search.

End of entry — will iterate after Samir's prototype results and the first 3 adjudication sessions.
